questions.stem: A chord $AB$ subtends an angle of $40°$ at the circumference in the major segment. What angle does it subtend at the circumference in the minor segment?
questions.explanation: The angles in the major and minor segments are supplementary (they add to $180°$), since $ABCD$ forms a cyclic quadrilateral when you take one point in each segment. So the angle in the minor segment is $180° - 40° = 140°$.

questions.stem: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord:

options.text: Passes through the midpoint of the arc only

questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord always bisects the chord (cuts it into two equal halves). This is a key circle theorem.

questions.stem: Two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are:
questions.explanation: Tangents drawn from the same external point to a circle are always equal in length. This can be proved using congruent triangles (RHS).
